Lead (Metal)
led
noun
Hebrew ophereth (H5777) — the dense, dull metal (Pb); appears in Scripture as the metal of WEIGHT (Exod 15:10), of dross (Ezek 22:18-20), of permanent inscription (Job 19:24), and most strikingly as the woman of wickedness sealed in an ephah with a talent of lead in Zechariah's vision (Zech 5:7-8).

📖 Biblical Definition

Lead in biblical theology is the metal of WEIGHT — heavy, dense, dragging downward. "They sank as lead in the mighty waters" (Exod 15:10) — Pharaoh's army at the Red Sea, sinking under the weight of God's judgment. Job longs for his words to be "graven with an iron pen and lead in the rock for ever" (Job 19:24) — lead was used to fill engraved letters in stone, making the inscription permanent and legible across centuries. Most striking is Zechariah's vision of the ephah (Zech 5:5-11): an ephah-basket appears, with a woman called "wickedness" sitting in it; "And he cast it into the midst of the ephah; and he cast the weight of lead upon the mouth thereof." The talent of lead seals wickedness inside the ephah, which is then carried to Shinar (Babylon) to be set up in a house. The image: wickedness, weighed down with the weight of lead, exiled to Babylon. Lead is also one of the metals listed as dross to be purged from God's people (Ezek 22:18-20) and the goods traded by Tarshish to Tyre (Ezek 27:12). Lead's biblical theology is consistent: it is the metal of HEAVINESS, of what cannot be lifted, of what sinks and weights and seals. The Pharaoh's army that hardened against Yahweh sank like lead. Wickedness in Zechariah's vision was sealed with lead. The dross alloyed in God's people will be burned with lead. The weight of God's judgments is captured in this single dull dense metal.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

A dense, dull metal (Pb); the metal of weight, dross, permanent inscription, and the sealed ephah of wickedness in Zechariah's vision.

LEAD, noun. A heavy, soft, malleable, bluish-gray metal (Pb); one of the densest of the common metals.

In Scripture, the metal of weight (Exod 15:10 — Pharaoh's army sinking like lead); permanent inscription (Job 19:24); dross (Ezek 22:18-20); the talent of lead sealing wickedness in Zechariah's ephah vision (Zech 5:7-8); the trade goods of Tarshish (Ezek 27:12).

📖 Key Scripture

Exodus 15:10 — "Thou didst blow with thy wind, the sea covered them: they sank as lead in the mighty waters."

Zechariah 5:7-8 — "And, behold, there was lifted up a talent of lead: and this is a woman that sitteth in the midst of the ephah. And he said, This is wickedness. And he cast it into the midst of the ephah; and he cast the weight of lead upon the mouth thereof."

Job 19:24 — "That they were graven with an iron pen and lead in the rock for ever!"

Ezekiel 22:18 — "Son of man, the house of Israel is to me become dross: all they are brass, and tin, and iron, and lead, in the midst of the furnace; they are even the dross of silver."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

Lead is corrupted when its biblical theology of weight and judgment is dismissed as material happenstance, or when Zechariah's lead-sealed-ephah vision is treated as obscure apocalyptic flourish rather than as the canonically clear picture of wickedness weighed down and sent to Babylon.

expand to see more

Weight-theology dismissal. "They sank as lead" (Exod 15:10) is sometimes treated as poetic flourish in the Song of Moses — pretty metaphor, nothing more. But the choice of metal is theological: lead is the densest common metal, the one that sinks fastest, the metal that cannot be lifted by lighter fluids. God's judgment on Pharaoh's army was lead-heavy; nothing could buoy them. The Song of Moses (Exod 15) is a victory song over a judgment that crushed an empire — the lead-image preaches the weight of what God does.

Zechariah-5 obscurity dismissal. Zechariah 5:5-11 — the ephah containing the woman called wickedness, sealed with a talent of lead, carried to Babylon — is one of the more obscure visions in the prophets, often skipped over in popular preaching. But the vision is sharp: wickedness has WEIGHT, must be SEALED, and must be exiled to Babylon (the canonical city of human pride against God). The talent of lead pictures the dead weight under which wickedness is permanently sealed. The vision is a comfort to God's people: He WILL seal wickedness, He will EXILE it, He will give it a house in Babylon — and Babylon will fall (Rev 18). The image is hopeful when read alongside Revelation.

Usage

"They sank as lead in the mighty waters — the weight of God's judgment on the empire that defied Him."

"A talent of lead seals wickedness inside the ephah, sent to Babylon: God knows how to weigh wickedness down and exile it."

"Lead is the metal of what sinks, what seals, what cannot be lifted — and what God uses to image the weight of His judgments."
